CHAPTER I

GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:
1. Regency Area is the Regency Area of Bekasi. 2. Regent is the Regent of Bekasi. 3. Regency Regional Government is the Regent as an element of regional government administration who leads the implementation of government affairs that are the authority of the autonomous region. 4. Regional Secretary is the Regional Secretary of Bekasi Regency. 5. Regional Apparatus is an auxiliary element of the Regent and Regional House of Representatives in government affairs that are the authority of the region. 6. Woman is a person of female gender starting from infants, adolescents, adults up to the elderly, who has been recognized by law. 7. Protection is all efforts aimed at providing a sense of security to women carried out by family, advocates, social institutions, police, prosecutors, courts or other parties either temporarily or based on court decisions. 8. Protection of Women is all activities aimed at providing a sense of security carried out by the Regional Government, community, and/or other parties who know or hear that violence against women will or has occurred. 9. Discrimination is any restriction, harassment or exclusion that is directly or indirectly based on human differentiation on the basis of religion, ethnicity, race, ethnic group, group, class, social status, economic status, gender, language, political beliefs, which results in the reduction, deviation or elimination of recognition, implementation or use of human rights and fundamental freedoms in life both individually and collectively in the political, economic, legal, educational, social, cultural and other aspects of life. 10. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband, wife, or husband, wife and their children, or father and children, or mother and children, or blood relatives in a straight line upward or downward up to the third degree. 11. Household is husband, wife, children, people who have family relationships due to blood relations, marriage, breastfeeding, care, and representation, and/or domestic workers and reside in that household. 12. Victim is a woman who experiences misery and/or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of violence and life vulnerability. 13. Violence is any act that results in or may result in misery or suffering either physically, psychologically, sexually, economically and socially as well as discrimination against victims that causes danger to life, body or results in the deprivation of a person's freedom. 14. Violence Against Women is any act that results in or may result in misery or suffering either physically, psychologically, sexually, socio-economically and discrimination, including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in public or private life. 15. Domestic Violence is any act against a person, especially women, that results in misery or suffering physically, sexually, psychologically and/or threats of domestic neglect including threats to commit acts of coercion or deprivation of freedom unlawfully within the scope of the household. 16. Physical Violence is any act that causes pain, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage, fainting and or causes death. 17. Psychological Violence is an act that causes fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or other psychological suffering to a person. 18. Sexual Violence is any act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, forced unnatural or unwanted sexual intercourse, forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and or certain other purposes. 19. Women's Rights are a set of rights inherent in a woman or group of people not to experience discrimination, misery or suffering either directly or indirectly committed by state apparatus or by the state or by regional government apparatus or individuals which are natural rights given by God Almighty. 20. Service is an action taken as soon as possible to victims when seeing, hearing and or knowing that violence against victims will, is or has occurred. 21. Integrated Service is a series of activities to provide protection for witnesses and victims of violence carried out jointly by relevant agencies or institutions as one unit of organizing health rehabilitation, social rehabilitation, repatriation, social reintegration, and legal assistance. 22. Disability is an individual who has physical or mental limitations. 23. Complaint is a series of actions taken by the organizer of the Integrated Service Center to follow up on reports of acts of violence against victims of violence. 24. Health Rehabilitation is the recovery of victims of violence from the health problems they suffer. 25. Social Rehabilitation is a service aimed at restoring the psychological condition and developing the ability of a person experiencing social dysfunction so that they can carry out their social functions properly. 26. Legal Assistance is legal services provided by assistants, law enforcement officers which include providing legal consultation, exercising power, representing, accompanying, defending and taking other legal actions for victims of violence. 27. Repatriation is an effort to return victims of violence from the receiving area/where violence occurred to the area of origin or family. 28. Social Reintegration is an effort to reunite victims of violence with family, community, institutions or other social environments that can provide protection. 29. Regional Technical Implementation Unit for the Protection of Women and Children, hereinafter abbreviated as UPTD PPA, is an institution established by the Regional Government to provide services to women and children who experience criminal and civil problems. 30. Safe House is a shelter for victims during the assistance process, for the safety and comfort of victims from threats and dangers of perpetrators. 31.

Article 12

Domestic Violence as referred to in Article 8 letter d is caused by:
a. acts that neglect women within the household by someone who is obliged to provide life, care or maintenance to such women;
b. acts that result in economic dependence by restricting and/or prohibiting decent work inside or outside the home so that the victim is under someone's control; and
c. acts committed by family members that result in pain, bruising, injury, wounds or defects on a person's body, miscarriage, fainting and/or causing death.

Article 33

1. In order to coordinate, synchronize policies, programs and activities for the protection of women to eliminate all forms of discrimination and acts of violence against women in the Region, the Regent establishes a task force, forum, working group or other institutions.
2. The membership of the task force, forum, working group or other institutions as referred to in paragraph (1) consists of related Regional Apparatus, community leaders, religious leaders, and universities.
3. Further provisions regarding the establishment of a task force, forum, working group or other institutions as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be regulated by the Regent.

CHAPTER VIII

COMMUNITY PARTICIPATION

Article 38

1. The community may participate in the implementation of women's protection in the region.
2. Participation as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be carried out by individuals, groups or social community organizations, non-governmental organizations, educational institutions, religious institutions, business entities and mass media.
3. Community participation as referred to in paragraph (1) may include:
a. providing information or reporting to the competent authority if aware of acts of violence against women;
b. taking preventive action against violence against women;
c. conducting skills training for women; and
d. establishing social community institutions that handle guidance and empowerment of women.
4. Further provisions regarding community participation as referred to in paragraph (2) shall be regulated by Regent Regulation.

CHAPTER IV

PREVENTION, PROTECTION SERVICES, AND EMPOWERMENT

Part One

Prevention of Violence Against Women

Article 5

Women victims of violence have the right to obtain protection, information, integrated services, continuous handling up to the rehabilitation stage and confidential handling from individuals, groups or institutions, both government and non-government.

CHAPTER VI

INSTITUTIONAL

Article 32

1. The Regional Government in an effort to provide and organize handling of protection services for women victims of violence, establishes the UPTD PPA.
2. The UPTD PPA as referred to in paragraph (1) is under and the regional apparatus is responsible to the head organizing government affairs in the field of women's empowerment and child protection.
3. The UPTD PPA as referred to in paragraph (2) has the duties of:
a. coordinating and synchronizing the handling of women's protection services in cooperation with related parties;
b. maintaining and developing networks and referral systems; and
c. coordinating, preparing and presenting reports on the protection of women.
4. The UPTD PPA as referred to in paragraph (1) is grouped into roles as follows:
a. health;
b. psychology;
c. social-education;
d. law; and
e. economy.
5. Further provisions regarding the establishment, main duties and functions as well as the management of the UPTD PPA as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be regulated by Regent Regulation.

Article 24

1. The implementation of women's empowerment in the field of health as referred to in Article 23 paragraph (2) letter a shall be implemented by the Regional Apparatus responsible for Health affairs.
2. The form of empowerment in the health field as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be in the form of health services to undergo reproductive life and sexual life that is healthy, safe, and free from coercion and/or violence.
3. Health services as referred to in paragraph (2) include:
a. Health services during the pre-pregnancy, pregnancy, childbirth and postpartum periods;
b. Pregnancy regulation, contraceptive services and sexual health;
c. Reproductive health services; and
d. Services and provision of adequate lactation rooms at every Regional government agency, public facilities and industries.
4. Health services as referred to in paragraph (2) shall be implemented through promotive, preventive, curative and rehabilitative approaches.

Part Four

Special Rights for the Protection of Women

Article 6

1. Women have the right to obtain special protection from matters that threaten their safety and/or health.
2. Special protection is given to women because their reproductive function is guaranteed and protected by law.
3. Special protection as referred to in paragraph (2) consists of health services related to:
a. menstruation;
b. pregnancy;
c. childbirth; and
d. breastfeeding
4. Health services as referred to in paragraph (3) may be provided by parties employing female workers in accordance with health service standards.

Article 21

Legal services as referred to in Article 16 letter e to assist victims in undergoing the judicial process by:
a. providing legal consultation that includes information regarding the rights of victims and the judicial process;
b. accompanying victims at the investigation, prosecution and examination levels in court hearings and assisting victims to fully describe the violence they experienced; and
c. coordinating with law enforcement apparatus, volunteer assistants and social workers so that the judicial process proceeds as it should.

Integrated Service is a series of activities to provide protection for witnesses and victims of violence carried out jointly by relevant agencies or institutions as one unit of organizing health rehabilitation, social rehabilitation, repatriation, social reintegration, and legal assistance. 22. Disability is an individual who has physical or mental limitations. 23. Complaint is a series of actions taken by the organizer of the Integrated Service Center to follow up on reports of acts of violence against victims of violence. 24. Health Rehabilitation is the recovery of victims of violence from the health problems they suffer. 25. Social Rehabilitation is a service aimed at restoring the psychological condition and developing the ability of a person experiencing social dysfunction so that they can carry out their social functions properly. 26. Legal Assistance is legal services provided by assistants, law enforcement officers which include providing legal consultation, exercising power, representing, accompanying, defending and taking other legal actions for victims of violence. 27. Repatriation is an effort to return victims of violence from the receiving area/where violence occurred to the area of origin or family. 28. Social Reintegration is an effort to reunite victims of violence with family, community, institutions or other social environments that can provide protection. 29. Regional Technical Implementation Unit for the Protection of Women and Children, hereinafter abbreviated as UPTD PPA, is an institution established by the Regional Government to provide services to women and children who experience criminal and civil problems. 30. Safe House is a shelter for victims during the assistance process, for the safety and comfort of victims from threats and dangers of perpetrators. 31.

Article 10

Psychological Violence as referred to in Article 8 letter b is caused by acts that result in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or severe psychological suffering in a person.

Article 20

1. Social rehabilitation services as referred to in Article 16 letter d shall be implemented by the UPTD PPA in the form of:
a. provision of spiritual guidance to victims; and
b. psychological recovery of victims.
2. Social rehabilitation services as referred to in paragraph (1) constitute services provided in order to restore the traumatic condition of victims, including the provision of safe houses to protect witnesses and victims from various threats and intimidation.

Article 9

Physical Violence as referred to in Article 8 letter a is caused by acts that result in pain, bruising, injury, wounds or defects on a person's body, miscarriage, fainting and/or causing death.

Article 12

Domestic Violence as referred to in Article 8 letter d is caused by:
a. acts that neglect women within the household by someone who is obliged to provide life, care or maintenance to such women;
b. acts that result in economic dependence by restricting and/or prohibiting decent work inside or outside the home so that the victim is under someone's control; and
c. acts committed by family members that result in pain, bruising, injury, wounds or defects on a person's body, miscarriage, fainting and/or causing death.

CHAPTER VI

INSTITUTIONAL

Article 32

1. The Regional Government in an effort to provide and organize handling of protection services for women victims of violence, establishes the UPTD PPA.
2. The UPTD PPA as referred to in paragraph (1) is under and the regional apparatus is responsible to the head organizing government affairs in the field of women's empowerment and child protection.
3. The UPTD PPA as referred to in paragraph (2) has the duties of:
a. coordinating and synchronizing the handling of women's protection services in cooperation with related parties;
b. maintaining and developing networks and referral systems; and
c. coordinating, preparing and presenting reports on the protection of women.
4. The UPTD PPA as referred to in paragraph (1) is grouped into roles as follows:
a. health;
b. psychology;
c. social-education;
d. law; and
e. economy.
5. Further provisions regarding the establishment, main duties and functions as well as the management of the UPTD PPA as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be regulated by Regent Regulation.

Part One

Prevention of Violence Against Women

Article 33

1. In order to coordinate, synchronize policies, programs and activities for the protection of women to eliminate all forms of discrimination and acts of violence against women in the Region, the Regent establishes a task force, forum, working group or other institutions.
2. The membership of the task force, forum, working group or other institutions as referred to in paragraph (1) consists of related Regional Apparatus, community leaders, religious leaders, and universities.
3. Further provisions regarding the establishment of a task force, forum, working group or other institutions as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be regulated by the Regent.

Article 5

Women victims of violence have the right to obtain protection, information, integrated services, continuous handling up to the rehabilitation stage and confidential handling from individuals, groups or institutions, both government and non-government.

CHAPTER VIII

COMMUNITY PARTICIPATION

Article 38

1. The community may participate in the implementation of women's protection in the region.
2. Participation as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be carried out by individuals, groups or social community organizations, non-governmental organizations, educational institutions, religious institutions, business entities and mass media.
3. Community participation as referred to in paragraph (1) may include:
a. providing information or reporting to the competent authority if aware of acts of violence against women;
b. taking preventive action against violence against women;
c. conducting skills training for women; and
d. establishing social community institutions that handle guidance and empowerment of women.
4. Further provisions regarding community participation as referred to in paragraph (2) shall be regulated by Regent Regulation.

Part Four

Special Rights for the Protection of Women

Article 21

Legal services as referred to in Article 16 letter e to assist victims in undergoing the judicial process by:
a. providing legal consultation that includes information regarding the rights of victims and the judicial process;
b. accompanying victims at the investigation, prosecution and examination levels in court hearings and assisting victims to fully describe the violence they experienced; and
c. coordinating with law enforcement apparatus, volunteer assistants and social workers so that the judicial process proceeds as it should.

Psychological Violence is an act that causes fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or other psychological suffering to a person. 18. Sexual Violence is any act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, forced unnatural or unwanted sexual intercourse, forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and or certain other purposes. 19. Integrated Service is a series of activities to provide protection for witnesses and victims of violence carried out jointly by relevant agencies or institutions as one unit of organizing health rehabilitation, social rehabilitation, repatriation, social reintegration, and legal assistance. 22. Complaint is a series of actions taken by the organizer of the Integrated Service Center to follow up on reports of acts of violence against victims of violence. 24. Social Reintegration is an effort to reunite victims of violence with family, community, institutions or other social environments that can provide protection. 29. Protection Services

Reporting

COMMUNITY PARTICIPATION

3. Monitoring as referred to in paragraph (2) shall be conducted periodically starting from planning up to the policies, programs and activities for the empowerment and protection of women for the current year.

INSTITUTIONAL

Article 32

Part One

Prevention of Violence Against Women

Article 21

Legal services as referred to in Article 16 letter e to assist victims in undergoing the judicial process by:
a. providing legal consultation that includes information regarding the rights of victims and the judicial process;

c. coordinating with law enforcement apparatus, volunteer assistants and social workers so that the judicial process proceeds as it should.

CHAPTER VIII

COMMUNITY PARTICIPATION

Article 38

1. The community may participate in the implementation of women's protection in the region.
2. Participation as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be carried out by individuals, groups or social community organizations, non-governmental organizations, educational institutions, religious institutions, business entities and mass media.
3. Community participation as referred to in paragraph (1) may include:
a. providing information or reporting to the competent authority if aware of acts of violence against women;
b. taking preventive action against violence against women;
c. conducting skills training for women; and
d. establishing social community institutions that handle guidance and empowerment of women.
4. Further provisions regarding community participation as referred to in paragraph (2) shall be regulated by Regent Regulation.

Article 36

1. To improve coordination of service delivery to women and children in the Region, UPTD PPA shall report the implementation of its duties to the Head of the Regional Agency responsible for Women's Empowerment and Child Protection with a copy to the Regent.
2. Reporting as referred to in paragraph (1) includes the implementation of handling women's protection issues in the Region.

Article 33

1. In order to coordinate, synchronize policies, programs and activities for the protection of women to eliminate all forms of discrimination and acts of violence against women in the Region, the Regent establishes a task force, forum, working group or other institutions.
2. The membership of the task force, forum, working group or other institutions as referred to in paragraph (1) consists of related Regional Apparatus, community leaders, religious leaders, and universities.
3. Further provisions regarding the establishment of a task force, forum, working group or other institutions as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be regulated by the Regent.

Article 24

1. The implementation of women's empowerment in the field of health as referred to in Article 23 paragraph (2) letter a shall be implemented by the Regional Apparatus responsible for Health affairs.
2. The form of empowerment in the health field as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be in the form of health services to undergo reproductive life and sexual life that is healthy, safe, and free from coercion and/or violence.
3. Health services as referred to in paragraph (2) include:
a. Health services during the pre-pregnancy, pregnancy, childbirth and postpartum periods;
b. Pregnancy regulation, contraceptive services and sexual health;
c. Reproductive health services; and
d. Services and provision of adequate lactation rooms at every Regional government agency, public facilities and industries.
4. Health services as referred to in paragraph (2) shall be implemented through promotive, preventive, curative and rehabilitative approaches.

Article 20

1. Social rehabilitation services as referred to in Article 16 letter d shall be implemented by the UPTD PPA in the form of:
a. provision of spiritual guidance to victims; and
b. psychological recovery of victims.
2. Social rehabilitation services as referred to in paragraph (1) constitute services provided in order to restore the traumatic condition of victims, including the provision of safe houses to protect witnesses and victims from various threats and intimidation.

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

Discrimination is any restriction, harassment or exclusion that is directly or indirectly based on human differentiation on the basis of religion, ethnicity, race, ethnic group, group, class, social status, economic status, gender, language, political beliefs, which results in the reduction, deviation or elimination of recognition, implementation or use of human rights and fundamental freedoms in life both individually and collectively in the political, economic, legal, educational, social, cultural and other aspects of life. 10. CHAPTER I

GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:
1. Regency Area is the Regency Area of Bekasi. 2. Regent is the Regent of Bekasi. 3. Regency Regional Government is the Regent as an element of regional government administration who leads the implementation of government affairs that are the authority of the autonomous region. 4. Regional Secretary is the Regional Secretary of Bekasi Regency. 5. Regional Apparatus is an auxiliary element of the Regent and Regional House of Representatives in government affairs that are the authority of the region. 6. Woman is a person of female gender starting from infants, adolescents, adults up to the elderly, who has been recognized by law. 7. Protection is all efforts aimed at providing a sense of security to women carried out by family, advocates, social institutions, police, prosecutors, courts or other parties either temporarily or based on court decisions. 8. Protection of Women is all activities aimed at providing a sense of security carried out by the Regional Government, community, and/or other parties who know or hear that violence against women will or has occurred. 9. Discrimination is any restriction, harassment or exclusion that is directly or indirectly based on human differentiation on the basis of religion, ethnicity, race, ethnic group, group, class, social status, economic status, gender, language, political beliefs, which results in the reduction, deviation or elimination of recognition, implementation or use of human rights and fundamental freedoms in life both individually and collectively in the political, economic, legal, educational, social, cultural and other aspects of life. 10. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband, wife, or husband, wife and their children, or father and children, or mother and children, or blood relatives in a straight line upward or downward up to the third degree. 11. Household is husband, wife, children, people who have family relationships due to blood relations, marriage, breastfeeding, care, and representation, and/or domestic workers and reside in that household. 12. Victim is a woman who experiences misery and/or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of violence and life vulnerability. 13. Violence is any act that results in or may result in misery or suffering either physically, psychologically, sexually, economically and socially as well as discrimination against victims that causes danger to life, body or results in the deprivation of a person's freedom. 14. Violence Against Women is any act that results in or may result in misery or suffering either physically, psychologically, sexually, socio-economically and discrimination, including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in public or private life. 15. Domestic Violence is any act against a person, especially women, that results in misery or suffering physically, sexually, psychologically and/or threats of domestic neglect including threats to commit acts of coercion or deprivation of freedom unlawfully within the scope of the household. 16. Physical Violence is any act that causes pain, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage, fainting and or causes death. 17. Psychological Violence is an act that causes fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or other psychological suffering to a person. 18. Sexual Violence is any act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, forced unnatural or unwanted sexual intercourse, forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and or certain other purposes. 19. Women's Rights are a set of rights inherent in a woman or group of people not to experience discrimination, misery or suffering either directly or indirectly committed by state apparatus or by the state or by regional government apparatus or individuals which are natural rights given by God Almighty. 20. Service is an action taken as soon as possible to victims when seeing, hearing and or knowing that violence against victims will, is or has occurred. 21. Integrated Service is a series of activities to provide protection for witnesses and victims of violence carried out jointly by relevant agencies or institutions as one unit of organizing health rehabilitation, social rehabilitation, repatriation, social reintegration, and legal assistance. 22. Disability is an individual who has physical or mental limitations. 23. Complaint is a series of actions taken by the organizer of the Integrated Service Center to follow up on reports of acts of violence against victims of violence. 24. Health Rehabilitation is the recovery of victims of violence from the health problems they suffer. 25. Social Rehabilitation is a service aimed at restoring the psychological condition and developing the ability of a person experiencing social dysfunction so that they can carry out their social functions properly. 26. Legal Assistance is legal services provided by assistants, law enforcement officers which include providing legal consultation, exercising power, representing, accompanying, defending and taking other legal actions for victims of violence. 27. Repatriation is an effort to return victims of violence from the receiving area/where violence occurred to the area of origin or family. 28. Social Reintegration is an effort to reunite victims of violence with family, community, institutions or other social environments that can provide protection. 29. Regional Technical Implementation Unit for the Protection of Women and Children, hereinafter abbreviated as UPTD PPA, is an institution established by the Regional Government to provide services to women and children who experience criminal and civil problems. 30. Safe House is a shelter for victims during the assistance process, for the safety and comfort of victims from threats and dangers of perpetrators. 31.

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

Protection is all efforts aimed at providing a sense of security to women carried out by family, advocates, social institutions, police, prosecutors, courts or other parties either temporarily or based on court decisions. 8. Protection of Women is all activities aimed at providing a sense of security carried out by the Regional Government, community, and/or other parties who know or hear that violence against women will or has occurred. 9. Discrimination is any restriction, harassment or exclusion that is directly or indirectly based on human differentiation on the basis of religion, ethnicity, race, ethnic group, group, class, social status, economic status, gender, language, political beliefs, which results in the reduction, deviation or elimination of recognition, implementation or use of human rights and fundamental freedoms in life both individually and collectively in the political, economic, legal, educational, social, cultural and other aspects of life. 10. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband, wife, or husband, wife and their children, or father and children, or mother and children, or blood relatives in a straight line upward or downward up to the third degree. 11. Household is husband, wife, children, people who have family relationships due to blood relations, marriage, breastfeeding, care, and representation, and/or domestic workers and reside in that household. 12. Victim is a woman who experiences misery and/or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of violence and life vulnerability. 13. Violence is any act that results in or may result in misery or suffering either physically, psychologically, sexually, economically and socially as well as discrimination against victims that causes danger to life, body or results in the deprivation of a person's freedom. 14. Violence Against Women is any act that results in or may result in misery or suffering either physically, psychologically, sexually, socio-economically and discrimination, including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in public or private life. 15. Domestic Violence is any act against a person, especially women, that results in misery or suffering physically, sexually, psychologically and/or threats of domestic neglect including threats to commit acts of coercion or deprivation of freedom unlawfully within the scope of the household. 16. Physical Violence is any act that causes pain, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage, fainting and or causes death. 17. Psychological Violence is an act that causes fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or other psychological suffering to a person. 18. Sexual Violence is any act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, forced unnatural or unwanted sexual intercourse, forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and or certain other purposes. 19. Women's Rights are a set of rights inherent in a woman or group of people not to experience discrimination, misery or suffering either directly or indirectly committed by state apparatus or by the state or by regional government apparatus or individuals which are natural rights given by God Almighty. 20. Service is an action taken as soon as possible to victims when seeing, hearing and or knowing that violence against victims will, is or has occurred. 21. Integrated Service is a series of activities to provide protection for witnesses and victims of violence carried out jointly by relevant agencies or institutions as one unit of organizing health rehabilitation, social rehabilitation, repatriation, social reintegration, and legal assistance. 22. Complaint is a series of actions taken by the organizer of the Integrated Service Center to follow up on reports of acts of violence against victims of violence. 24. Social Rehabilitation is a service aimed at restoring the psychological condition and developing the ability of a person experiencing social dysfunction so that they can carry out their social functions properly. 26. Repatriation is an effort to return victims of violence from the receiving area/where violence occurred to the area of origin or family. 28. Social Reintegration is an effort to reunite victims of violence with family, community, institutions or other social environments that can provide protection. 29. Regional Technical Implementation Unit for the Protection of Women and Children, hereinafter abbreviated as UPTD PPA, is an institution established by the Regional Government to provide services to women and children who experience criminal and civil problems. 30. Safe House is a shelter for victims during the assistance process, for the safety and comfort of victims from threats and dangers of perpetrators. 31.

GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1

Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband, wife, or husband, wife and their children, or father and children, or mother and children, or blood relatives in a straight line upward or downward up to the third degree. 11. Physical Violence is any act that causes pain, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage, fainting and or causes death. 17. Psychological Violence is an act that causes fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or other psychological suffering to a person. 18. Sexual Violence is any act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, forced unnatural or unwanted sexual intercourse, forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and or certain other purposes. 19. Repatriation is an effort to return victims of violence from the receiving area/where violence occurred to the area of origin or family. 28. Social Reintegration is an effort to reunite victims of violence with family, community, institutions or other social environments that can provide protection. 29. Regional Technical Implementation Unit for the Protection of Women and Children, hereinafter abbreviated as UPTD PPA, is an institution established by the Regional Government to provide services to women and children who experience criminal and civil problems. 30. Safe House is a shelter for victims during the assistance process, for the safety and comfort of victims from threats and dangers of perpetrators. 31.

a. Health services during the pre-pregnancy, pregnancy, childbirth and postpartum periods;
b. Pregnancy regulation, contraceptive services and sexual health;
c. Reproductive health services; and
d. Services and provision of adequate lactation rooms at every Regional government agency, public facilities and industries.

CHAPTER I

GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:
1. Regency Area is the Regency Area of Bekasi. 2. Regent is the Regent of Bekasi. 3. Regency Regional Government is the Regent as an element of regional government administration who leads the implementation of government affairs that are the authority of the autonomous region. 4. Regional Secretary is the Regional Secretary of Bekasi Regency. 5. Regional Apparatus is an auxiliary element of the Regent and Regional House of Representatives in government affairs that are the authority of the region. 6. Woman is a person of female gender starting from infants, adolescents, adults up to the elderly, who has been recognized by law. 7. Protection is all efforts aimed at providing a sense of security to women carried out by family, advocates, social institutions, police, prosecutors, courts or other parties either temporarily or based on court decisions. 8. Protection of Women is all activities aimed at providing a sense of security carried out by the Regional Government, community, and/or other parties who know or hear that violence against women will or has occurred. 9. Discrimination is any restriction, harassment or exclusion that is directly or indirectly based on human differentiation on the basis of religion, ethnicity, race, ethnic group, group, class, social status, economic status, gender, language, political beliefs, which results in the reduction, deviation or elimination of recognition, implementation or use of human rights and fundamental freedoms in life both individually and collectively in the political, economic, legal, educational, social, cultural and other aspects of life. 10. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband, wife, or husband, wife and their children, or father and children, or mother and children, or blood relatives in a straight line upward or downward up to the third degree. 11. Household is husband, wife, children, people who have family relationships due to blood relations, marriage, breastfeeding, care, and representation, and/or domestic workers and reside in that household. 12. Victim is a woman who experiences misery and/or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of violence and life vulnerability. 13. Violence is any act that results in or may result in misery or suffering either physically, psychologically, sexually, economically and socially as well as discrimination against victims that causes danger to life, body or results in the deprivation of a person's freedom. 14. Violence Against Women is any act that results in or may result in misery or suffering either physically, psychologically, sexually, socio-economically and discrimination, including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in public or private life. 15. Domestic Violence is any act against a person, especially women, that results in misery or suffering physically, sexually, psychologically and/or threats of domestic neglect including threats to commit acts of coercion or deprivation of freedom unlawfully within the scope of the household. 16. Physical Violence is any act that causes pain, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage, fainting and or causes death. 17. Psychological Violence is an act that causes fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or other psychological suffering to a person. 18. Sexual Violence is any act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, forced unnatural or unwanted sexual intercourse, forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and or certain other purposes. 19. Women's Rights are a set of rights inherent in a woman or group of people not to experience discrimination, misery or suffering either directly or indirectly committed by state apparatus or by the state or by regional government apparatus or individuals which are natural rights given by God Almighty. 20. Service is an action taken as soon as possible to victims when seeing, hearing and or knowing that violence against victims will, is or has occurred. 21. Integrated Service is a series of activities to provide protection for witnesses and victims of violence carried out jointly by relevant agencies or institutions as one unit of organizing health rehabilitation, social rehabilitation, repatriation, social reintegration, and legal assistance. 22. Disability is an individual who has physical or mental limitations. 23. Complaint is a series of actions taken by the organizer of the Integrated Service Center to follow up on reports of acts of violence against victims of violence. 24. Health Rehabilitation is the recovery of victims of violence from the health problems they suffer. 25. Social Rehabilitation is a service aimed at restoring the psychological condition and developing the ability of a person experiencing social dysfunction so that they can carry out their social functions properly. 26. Legal Assistance is legal services provided by assistants, law enforcement officers which include providing legal consultation, exercising power, representing, accompanying, defending and taking other legal actions for victims of violence. 27. Repatriation is an effort to return victims of violence from the receiving area/where violence occurred to the area of origin or family. 28. Social Reintegration is an effort to reunite victims of violence with family, community, institutions or other social environments that can provide protection. 29. Regional Technical Implementation Unit for the Protection of Women and Children, hereinafter abbreviated as UPTD PPA, is an institution established by the Regional Government to provide services to women and children who experience criminal and civil problems. 30. Safe House is a shelter for victims during the assistance process, for the safety and comfort of victims from threats and dangers of perpetrators. 31.

1. Regency Area is the Regency Area of Bekasi. 2. Regent is the Regent of Bekasi. 3. Regency Regional Government is the Regent as an element of regional government administration who leads the implementation of government affairs that are the authority of the autonomous region. 4. Regional Secretary is the Regional Secretary of Bekasi Regency. 5. Regional Apparatus is an auxiliary element of the Regent and Regional House of Representatives in government affairs that are the authority of the region. 6. Woman is a person of female gender starting from infants, adolescents, adults up to the elderly, who has been recognized by law. 7. Protection is all efforts aimed at providing a sense of security to women carried out by family, advocates, social institutions, police, prosecutors, courts or other parties either temporarily or based on court decisions. 8. Protection of Women is all activities aimed at providing a sense of security carried out by the Regional Government, community, and/or other parties who know or hear that violence against women will or has occurred. 9. Discrimination is any restriction, harassment or exclusion that is directly or indirectly based on human differentiation on the basis of religion, ethnicity, race, ethnic group, group, class, social status, economic status, gender, language, political beliefs, which results in the reduction, deviation or elimination of recognition, implementation or use of human rights and fundamental freedoms in life both individually and collectively in the political, economic, legal, educational, social, cultural and other aspects of life. 10. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband, wife, or husband, wife and their children, or father and children, or mother and children, or blood relatives in a straight line upward or downward up to the third degree. 11. Household is husband, wife, children, people who have family relationships due to blood relations, marriage, breastfeeding, care, and representation, and/or domestic workers and reside in that household. 12. Victim is a woman who experiences misery and/or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of violence and life vulnerability. 13. Violence is any act that results in or may result in misery or suffering either physically, psychologically, sexually, economically and socially as well as discrimination against victims that causes danger to life, body or results in the deprivation of a person's freedom. 14. Violence Against Women is any act that results in or may result in misery or suffering either physically, psychologically, sexually, socio-economically and discrimination, including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in public or private life. 15. Domestic Violence is any act against a person, especially women, that results in misery or suffering physically, sexually, psychologically and/or threats of domestic neglect including threats to commit acts of coercion or deprivation of freedom unlawfully within the scope of the household. 16. Physical Violence is any act that causes pain, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage, fainting and or causes death. 17. Psychological Violence is an act that causes fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or other psychological suffering to a person. 18. Sexual Violence is any act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, forced unnatural or unwanted sexual intercourse, forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and or certain other purposes. 19. Women's Rights are a set of rights inherent in a woman or group of people not to experience discrimination, misery or suffering either directly or indirectly committed by state apparatus or by the state or by regional government apparatus or individuals which are natural rights given by God Almighty. 20. Service is an action taken as soon as possible to victims when seeing, hearing and or knowing that violence against victims will, is or has occurred. 21. Integrated Service is a series of activities to provide protection for witnesses and victims of violence carried out jointly by relevant agencies or institutions as one unit of organizing health rehabilitation, social rehabilitation, repatriation, social reintegration, and legal assistance. 22. Disability is an individual who has physical or mental limitations. 23. Complaint is a series of actions taken by the organizer of the Integrated Service Center to follow up on reports of acts of violence against victims of violence. 24. Health Rehabilitation is the recovery of victims of violence from the health problems they suffer. 25. Social Rehabilitation is a service aimed at restoring the psychological condition and developing the ability of a person experiencing social dysfunction so that they can carry out their social functions properly. 26. Legal Assistance is legal services provided by assistants, law enforcement officers which include providing legal consultation, exercising power, representing, accompanying, defending and taking other legal actions for victims of violence. 27. Repatriation is an effort to return victims of violence from the receiving area/where violence occurred to the area of origin or family. 28. Social Reintegration is an effort to reunite victims of violence with family, community, institutions or other social environments that can provide protection. 29. Regional Technical Implementation Unit for the Protection of Women and Children, hereinafter abbreviated as UPTD PPA, is an institution established by the Regional Government to provide services to women and children who experience criminal and civil problems. 30. Safe House is a shelter for victims during the assistance process, for the safety and comfort of victims from threats and dangers of perpetrators. 31.

Article 22

1. Repatriation and social reintegration services as referred to in Article 16 letter f aim to return victims to their families and social environment;
2. Repatriation and social reintegration services as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be carried out by the Regional Government in coordination with:
a. district/city governments within one provincial area; and
b. related agencies and institutions both governmental and non-governmental.

CHAPTER VIII

COMMUNITY PARTICIPATION

Article 38

1. The community may participate in the implementation of women's protection in the region.
2. Participation as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be carried out by individuals, groups or social community organizations, non-governmental organizations, educational institutions, religious institutions, business entities and mass media.
3. Community participation as referred to in paragraph (1) may include:
a. providing information or reporting to the competent authority if aware of acts of violence against women;
b. taking preventive action against violence against women;
c. conducting skills training for women; and
d. establishing social community institutions that handle guidance and empowerment of women.
4. Further provisions regarding community participation as referred to in paragraph (2) shall be regulated by Regent Regulation.

CHAPTER VI

INSTITUTIONAL

Article 32

1. The Regional Government in an effort to provide and organize handling of protection services for women victims of violence, establishes the UPTD PPA.
2. The UPTD PPA as referred to in paragraph (1) is under and the regional apparatus is responsible to the head organizing government affairs in the field of women's empowerment and child protection.
3. The UPTD PPA as referred to in paragraph (2) has the duties of:
a. coordinating and synchronizing the handling of women's protection services in cooperation with related parties;
b. maintaining and developing networks and referral systems; and
c. coordinating, preparing and presenting reports on the protection of women.
4. The UPTD PPA as referred to in paragraph (1) is grouped into roles as follows:
a. health;
b. psychology;
c. social-education;
d. law; and
e. economy.
5. Further provisions regarding the establishment, main duties and functions as well as the management of the UPTD PPA as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be regulated by Regent Regulation.

Article 36

2. Reporting as referred to in paragraph (1) includes the implementation of handling women's protection issues in the Region.

Further provisions regarding supervision, evaluation, and reporting of policies, programs, and activities for Women's Protection as referred to in Article 34 through Article 36 shall be regulated by Regent Regulation.

Article 33

1. In order to coordinate, synchronize policies, programs and activities for the protection of women to eliminate all forms of discrimination and acts of violence against women in the Region, the Regent establishes a task force, forum, working group or other institutions.
2. The membership of the task force, forum, working group or other institutions as referred to in paragraph (1) consists of related Regional Apparatus, community leaders, religious leaders, and universities.
3. Further provisions regarding the establishment of a task force, forum, working group or other institutions as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be regulated by the Regent.

Article 6

1. Women have the right to obtain special protection from matters that threaten their safety and/or health.
2. Special protection is given to women because their reproductive function is guaranteed and protected by law.
3. Special protection as referred to in paragraph (2) consists of health services related to:
a. menstruation;
b. pregnancy;
c. childbirth; and
d. breastfeeding
4. Health services as referred to in paragraph (3) may be provided by parties employing female workers in accordance with health service standards.

2. Empowerment of women in the field of government politics as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be implemented in accordance with laws and regulations.

CHAPTER I

GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:
1. Regency Area is the Regency Area of Bekasi. 2. Regent is the Regent of Bekasi. 3. Regency Regional Government is the Regent as an element of regional government administration who leads the implementation of government affairs that are the authority of the autonomous region. 4. Regional Secretary is the Regional Secretary of Bekasi Regency. 5. Regional Apparatus is an auxiliary element of the Regent and Regional House of Representatives in government affairs that are the authority of the region. 6. Woman is a person of female gender starting from infants, adolescents, adults up to the elderly, who has been recognized by law. 7. Protection is all efforts aimed at providing a sense of security to women carried out by family, advocates, social institutions, police, prosecutors, courts or other parties either temporarily or based on court decisions. 8. Protection of Women is all activities aimed at providing a sense of security carried out by the Regional Government, community, and/or other parties who know or hear that violence against women will or has occurred. 9. Discrimination is any restriction, harassment or exclusion that is directly or indirectly based on human differentiation on the basis of religion, ethnicity, race, ethnic group, group, class, social status, economic status, gender, language, political beliefs, which results in the reduction, deviation or elimination of recognition, implementation or use of human rights and fundamental freedoms in life both individually and collectively in the political, economic, legal, educational, social, cultural and other aspects of life. 10. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband, wife, or husband, wife and their children, or father and children, or mother and children, or blood relatives in a straight line upward or downward up to the third degree. 11. Household is husband, wife, children, people who have family relationships due to blood relations, marriage, breastfeeding, care, and representation, and/or domestic workers and reside in that household. 12. Victim is a woman who experiences misery and/or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of violence and life vulnerability. 13. Violence is any act that results in or may result in misery or suffering either physically, psychologically, sexually, economically and socially as well as discrimination against victims that causes danger to life, body or results in the deprivation of a person's freedom. 14. Violence Against Women is any act that results in or may result in misery or suffering either physically, psychologically, sexually, socio-economically and discrimination, including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in public or private life. 15. Domestic Violence is any act against a person, especially women, that results in misery or suffering physically, sexually, psychologically and/or threats of domestic neglect including threats to commit acts of coercion or deprivation of freedom unlawfully within the scope of the household. 16. Physical Violence is any act that causes pain, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage, fainting and or causes death. 17. Psychological Violence is an act that causes fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or other psychological suffering to a person. 18. Sexual Violence is any act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, forced unnatural or unwanted sexual intercourse, forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and or certain other purposes. 19. Women's Rights are a set of rights inherent in a woman or group of people not to experience discrimination, misery or suffering either directly or indirectly committed by state apparatus or by the state or by regional government apparatus or individuals which are natural rights given by God Almighty. 20. Service is an action taken as soon as possible to victims when seeing, hearing and or knowing that violence against victims will, is or has occurred. 21. Integrated Service is a series of activities to provide protection for witnesses and victims of violence carried out jointly by relevant agencies or institutions as one unit of organizing health rehabilitation, social rehabilitation, repatriation, social reintegration, and legal assistance. 22. Disability is an individual who has physical or mental limitations. 23. Complaint is a series of actions taken by the organizer of the Integrated Service Center to follow up on reports of acts of violence against victims of violence. 24. Health Rehabilitation is the recovery of victims of violence from the health problems they suffer. 25. Social Rehabilitation is a service aimed at restoring the psychological condition and developing the ability of a person experiencing social dysfunction so that they can carry out their social functions properly. 26. Legal Assistance is legal services provided by assistants, law enforcement officers which include providing legal consultation, exercising power, representing, accompanying, defending and taking other legal actions for victims of violence. 27. Repatriation is an effort to return victims of violence from the receiving area/where violence occurred to the area of origin or family. 28. Social Reintegration is an effort to reunite victims of violence with family, community, institutions or other social environments that can provide protection. 29. Regional Technical Implementation Unit for the Protection of Women and Children, hereinafter abbreviated as UPTD PPA, is an institution established by the Regional Government to provide services to women and children who experience criminal and civil problems. 30. Safe House is a shelter for victims during the assistance process, for the safety and comfort of victims from threats and dangers of perpetrators. 31.
